title: Closure Under Sums
statement: Let $T_1,T_2:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be exponential-polynomial functions, meaning that each is bounded by $2^{K(n+1)^k}$ for all $n$ and some natural-number constants $K,k$. Then the function $n\mapsto T_1(n)+T_2(n)$ is exponential-polynomial.
replaced:
Let $T_1, T_2 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ both be exponential-polynomial, i.e.\ each is
bounded by $2^{K(n+1)^k}$ for all $n$ and some constants $K, k \in \mathbb{N}$. Then the sum
$n \mapsto T_1(n) + T_2(n)$ is exponential-polynomial.
